Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute: MAR 2018 - Enhanced with specific details on how to perform the retrospective and added Agile specific role assignments

Review and understand, at least once per sprint:

  • How the team is performing work
  • What the interactions are between the team and stakeholders
  • What is impacting the team's ability to perform work
  • What is the impact of people, processes, tools and technologies on the project

In order to perform the sprint retrospective, make sure to:

  • Decide on a theme - Select a point of focus for the meeting. For example, if anything severely impacted the team's ability to complete work during the sprint this should be highlighted as a key topic of discussion, or theme, for the retrospective.
  • Agree on a date, time and participants - Typically the meeting is held after the sprint review meeting, toward the end of the sprint, with the entire team.
  • Select a facilitator - Most commonly, the Scrum Master facilitates the retrospective. However, the Scrum Master may opt to participate instead so as to share insights and allow another impartial Scrum Master to facilitate.
  • Send invitations, book a room and secure materials - The retrospective leader/facilitator should send invitations to all participants so the meeting starts on time. Next, secure an appropriate area to perform the retrospective. Select a venue that is relatively quiet and comfortable to support openness and sharing. Finally, check that any necessary supplies (i.e., flipcharts, post-its, markers, whiteboards) will be available for use during the meeting if needed.

• Structure the meeting carefully so it flows well, starting with a clear opening through to the definition and recording of actions at the end.
  • Use engaging and fun activities throughout the session to keep the energy level and engagement of the participants high.
  • Vary activities from one retrospective to the next so these regular meetings stay fresh and continue to challenge the attendees to question their perspectives.
  • Be tenacious when finalizing the list of actionable tasks at the end of the meeting so that it is small and concrete. The agreed upon actions are the true value of the meeting as they will reflect the necessary adaptations the team will need to make in order to improve.
  • Be sure to help the team follow through on the agreed actions; no matter how good the plan is it will not bring any value if it is not enacted.
  • Hold retrospectives at least once per sprint, more if deemed necessary by the Scrum Master and Product Owner.
To identify and understand areas for improvement in future sprints and document supporting actions if necessary.

section.name: Additional Information
section.rte: Remember to time-box the sprint retrospective meeting to no more than 3 hours for 4 week long sprint. The retrospective may be made shorter for shorter sprints.

Element.Name: Set the stage
Element.copyright:
© 2012, 2022 EYGM Limited. All Rights Reserved.
Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute: Open the retrospective by welcoming everyone and reiterating the purpose of the meeting. If a theme has been designated share the selected topic for discussion with the participants. It is also good practice to encourage active participation by asking a simple question to get discussion started and open the meeting up to the participants. For example, ask the group to describe their feelings about the last sprint in one or two words.

Element.Name: Gather data
Element.copyright:
© 2012, 2022 EYGM Limited. All Rights Reserved.
Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute: Give each team member an opportunity to share their experiences and observations from the last sprint. Encourage the team to identify specific pain points and key success factors, be sure to document these details. Make sure the team does not progress to the next step until a common understanding has been reached about the sprint. Topics for discussion may include roles, responsibilities, processes, practices, tools, communication channels, technology, etc.

Element.Name: Generate insights
Element.copyright:
© 2012, 2022 EYGM Limited. All Rights Reserved.
Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute: Guide the team in identifying what caused the sprint to be what it was by considering root causes. Review conditions, interactions or patterns in the data gathered in the previous step. The team can employ a number of methods to perform this diagnosis including a fish-bone diagram or 5-whys analysis. Regardless of the method, aim to obtain agreement among the team as to the root causes and significant events that impacted their ability to perform work (either positively or negatively) during the sprint. Steer the team away from generating solutions in this part of the meeting.

Element.Name: Decide on actions
Element.copyright:
© 2012, 2022 EYGM Limited. All Rights Reserved.
Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute: Have the team select one to three topics from the previous step for which they can begin to generate solutions. Brainstorm solutions and changes for the selected topics and guide the team in identifying specific, meaningful and realistic actions to improve the next sprint. Make sure the team agrees upon all actionable improvements to be made for the next sprint.

Element.Name: Close the retrospective
Element.copyright:
© 2012, 2022 EYGM Limited. All Rights Reserved.
Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute: Close the meeting by thanking everyone for their time, effort and ideas. Recap the key takeaways, lessons learned and action items that were discussed during the meeting. Revisit any action items agreed to for the next sprint to confirm alignment and ownership of these items. Help the team understand how they will retain the results of the retrospective and follow up on any actions. If applicable, document any actions from the retrospective as new Backlog Items to be considered for prioritization during the next sprint planning meeting.

Element.Name: manage_proj_agile
Element.attribute: Manage the full project lifecycle using a Scrum based Agile framework.

Element.Name: execute_sprints
Element.attribute: Initiate delivery via iterative sprints. The scope for each sprint will be individually assessed, evaluated, selected and executed. While the scope for each sprint will vary, the structure of the tasks will remain relatively constant starting with sprint planning through to the sprint retrospective.

Element.Name: execute_build_cycles_1_n
Element.attribute: Set of activities and tasks to be performed by the Development workstream while executing build iterations 1-n, spanning from planning for each sprint through unit testing custom components.

Element.Name: conduct_iteration_demo
Element.attribute: Review and present incrementally completed builds to project stakeholders; capture feedback and sign-offs from key stakeholders for completion of work.

Element.Name: progressive_build
Element.attribute: Iterate through the build cycles and drive business acceptance through incremental demos to key client stakeholders. Execute mock conversions and and prepare for system integration and user acceptance testing. Manage stakeholder engagement and communications around the change.

Element.Name: execute_build_cycles_1_n
Element.attribute: Iterate through the build cycles by planning for each sprint, defining the technical and integration specifications and data conversion scripts and completing the configurations and development. Validate the builds and conduct demos with the client.

Element.Name: conduct_iteration_demo
Element.attribute: Review and present incrementally completed builds to project stakeholders; capture feedback and sign-offs from key stakeholders for completion of work.
